cast_dialogue.linea: 'Get' is the most democratic verb in English, heroes: it changes meaning with every particle, and it lives in every conversation.
I got back from my trip last night and I'm still getting over the jet lag.
My girlfriend and I get along really well. We got to know each other at a cooking class.
I got up late, got on the bus just in time, and got off two stops early to buy fresh bread.
When we get together, we get through two pots of coffee! And yes, mis héroes, I'm getting older — but better.

She got over the flu quickly.
They got to know each other at school.
I didn't get on the last bus.
He hasn't got over the break-up yet.
We don't get along with the neighbours.
What time did you get home?
Did you get through the whole book?
How do you get along with your colleagues?
Did you get my message? Yes, I did.
Has she got over the flu? No, she hasn't.
Did they get back on time? Yes, they did.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: 'Get' + particle covers daily life: movement (get on/off, get back), change of state (get better, get older, get dressed), relationships (get along, get together, get to know) and recovery (get over, get through). Note: 'get over' is inseparable — 'I got over it'.

filas: get up, get on/off, get back
I got off two stops early.
get better, get angry, get wet
get along, get together, get to know

ejercicios.pregunta: Describe your typical morning and a recent reunion using four phrasal verbs with 'get'.
ejercicios.respuesta: I get up at seven and get dressed quickly. Last Friday we got together and I got home very late.

guion: Abuela Carmen: Sofía! You're late. What time did you get up?
Sofía: Too late! I got dressed in two minutes and got on the bus just in time.
Abuela Carmen: And why did you get off two stops early?
Sofía: To buy fresh bread for you! How are you getting along with the new neighbours?
Abuela Carmen: Very well! They're helping me get rid of the old furniture.
Sofía: And when did Ben get back from his trip?
Abuela Carmen: Last night. He's still getting over the jet lag.

reading.texto: Sofía got up late, got dressed quickly, and got on the bus just in time. She got off two stops early to get some fresh bread. At Abuela Carmen's house, everyone got together to get over the stress of the week. They got through two pots of coffee while getting to know Kenji's new girlfriend. When Ben got back from his trip, the party was still getting better.

preguntas.afirmacion: The friends drank two pots of coffee.
